Hi Sara / Jordan,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, attached is a concise capacity blueprint (PDF) that lays out three reservation options mapped to the workload profile you shared: baseline inference, peak-batch transcription, and nightly retrain jobs. High-level summary below — full details are in the attachment.

Option A — Conservative (lowest committed floor)
- Cluster size: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Min guaranteed: 8 GPUs (cold start protected)
- Ramp: 8 -> 16 over 90 days; staged activation in 3 x 30-day windows
- Includes 50k warm-token credits to smooth model cache warmups
- Pricing: blended reserved + usage (see PDF)

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
- Cluster size: 32 GPUs
- Min guaranteed: 16 GPUs
- Ramp: 16 -> 32 over 60 days; 2 x 30-day activations with burst lanes
- Includes 150k warm-token credits and priority placement during bursts

Option C — Aggressive (throughput-first)
- Cluster size: 64 GPUs
- Min guaranteed: 32 GPUs
- Ramp: 32 -> 64 over 30 days; supports sustained burst windows

Tradeoffs: min-guarantee reduces unit cost and ensures capacity during peaks but increases committed spend. We note based on your traffic shape the Balanced option (B) gives a ~25% lower unit cost vs A with predictable latency; C is only recommended if you expect sustained peak-level traffic beyond Q4.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which option (A/B/C) you want priced with a 12- or 24-month term.
2) If you want blended ramp activation we can map months to calendar dates and lock a do-not-decommit window.
3) I can route a DocuSign proposal once terms are agreed; or we can set up a quick call to walk through the attachment.

Attachment: redwood_capacity_blueprint_v1.pdf (4 pages)

Best,

Sara — thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers inline and I've looped Karthik (SE) and Marissa (AE) to help with calendar mapping and contracting.

1) "Min guaranteed": operationally this is the floor Redwood commits to keep warm and schedulable for your fleet.
- Preemption: none for the guaranteed floor during normal operations — only in rare, declared emergency maintenance windows (we provide 72h notice).
- Billing: you are billed at the committed rate for the floor (monthly), additional consumed capacity above the floor is billed at on-demand/overage rates.
- Availability: SLA applies to the floor; latency SLOs measured at token-level for requests routed to the guaranteed pool.

2) Calendar mapping: yes — we can anchor ramp start to the contract signature date. Example (if signed Jun 1): Option B -> 16 GPUs active on Jun 1, additional 16 activate on Jul 1. We can also offer a 2-week early-burst window if you need to start heavy testing.

3) Warm-token credits: they apply platform-wide (generation, chat, and embeddings) and are consumed at the same token accounting rate; we can earmark a portion specifically for embedding-heavy jobs if you prefer.

I'll draft a calendar-mapped variant and a DocuSign-ready proposal and circulate for internal approval.

Naomi

Background / ask:
- Customer leaning toward Option B but wants calendar-mapped activations tied to Q3 budgets. They asked us to clarify min-guarantee behavior and the token credits.
- Procurement will need SOC2 addendum + a short supplier questionnaire.

Proposal (my suggestion for what's approvable by sales):
1) Offer "Balanced (B) — Calendar variant": 32 GPU cluster, 16 GPU min-guarantee.
  - Ramp: 16 -> 32; 1st activation at signature, 2nd activation 30 days after.
  - Add a 60-day early-burst window for testing (no additional charge for bursts under 300k tokens).
2) Reduce committed floor exposure by 10% on pricing calculus (concession) in exchange for 12-month minimum term and 60-day irrevocable early phase-out notice (reduces reopen risk).
3) Provide dedicated warm-token pool of 150k tokens and a one-time migration credit of $10k to offset initial cache warmup and eval runs.

- Marissa: is a 10% concession on floor pricing OK from commission/discount policy? If not, propose alternative trade.
- Grace: approve the one-time migration credit up to $10k?
